findings.rationale: Local calibration is off: observed prevalence 0.2397 vs mean predicted 0.1696 (CITL -0.070, citl z=-5.2, ECE z=+3.8, prevalence z=+3.1) while local AUC is normal (0.801), so outcomes are higher than the features imply. Its updates are the most anomalous in the federation: median norm ratio 2.11 (z=+5.2) and mean cosine -0.04 against the median. The per-round trace shows the norm rising steadily and the cosine turning negative from about round 7 (-0.81 by round 19), which is the pattern a client pushing its intercept against the converged federation would produce. Calibration is negative in most rounds from round 1. Subgroup Sex=1 O/E 1.44 is a supporting signal.

Observed prevalence 0.1901 vs mean predicted 0.1395 (CITL -0.051, citl z=-4.1) with normal AUC (0.820). Update norms are large (median ratio 2.45, z=+3.5) and the cosine against the median turns negative from round 9 onward, reaching -0.54 by round 20. Over-observed outcomes appear in both Sex groups (O/E 1.51 and 1.40, z about 3.6 and 3.9), which fits a calibration gap rather than under-diagnosis. The client-level calibration evidence is moderate, so confidence is lower than for AZ.

Weaker lead. Observed prevalence 0.1789 vs mean predicted 0.1294 (CITL -0.050, citl z=-3.8) with normal AUC (0.820). Updates show a sustained rise in norm (about 1.8 by round 20) and negative cosine from about round 8, with cosine below zero in rounds 13-20 (mean cos 0.04 over the run). The income-subgroup outlier did not replicate on re-check, so it is not used as evidence. Reported only as a low-confidence lead.

report.summary: Screened all 52 clients (updates, local performance, drift, feature tails, subgroup outcomes by Sex, AgeGroup and Income), then confirmed suspects with narrower queries. Three clients show a consistent pattern: observed outcome prevalence above what the model predicts (negative CITL) with normal AUC, plus updates whose norm grows and whose cosine turns negative against the median over later rounds. That points to prevalence shift rather than poisoning, since local discrimination is normal. AZ is the strongest case (confidence 0.8). WA is moderate (0.55). UT is a weak lead (0.35). Other flags (HighChol tails in NC/NM/VI/WV, DC BMI, GU Sex and PhysActivity tails, AgeGroup/Income subgroup outliers in ME/OH/NV/GA/WV/NC) were either small-client noise or did not replicate on re-check, so they are not reported. No drift, label-noise, missing-artefact, subgroup-bias or explanation-instability signal stood out clearly. Budget is fully spent (20.0 used).
